subject: Live conversation delay — guidance and temporary client checklist
messages:
From: Rita Chen <rita.chen@novusretail.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-team@novusretail.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Live sessions sporadically slow — hitting timeouts on streaming chat

Hi Priya,

We started seeing intermittent delays this morning across our web live-chat widget. Some user sessions will stream for several seconds with long pauses between chunks, and in a few cases our client hits a 30s application timeout and shows a failure.

Impact: ~5% of conversations in the last hour; some high-value customers noticed. We rolled back a recent front-end change and saw no immediate improvement.

Can you confirm whether this is known on Redwood's side? If there are recommended client-side fallbacks we should enable quickly, please share — we need a checklist to reduce end-user failures while you investigate.

I've attached a short diagnostic excerpt from our SDK logs where the stream stalls (diagnostic_snippet_0514.txt).

Thanks — Rita
Rita Chen
Head of Customer Ops, Novus Retail
rita.chen@novusretail.com

--- attachment: diagnostic_snippet_0514.txt (log snippet)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Rita Chen <rita.chen@novusretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live sessions sporadically slow — hitting timeouts on streaming chat

Hi Rita — thanks for the report and the log snippet. We see a handful of similar reports coming in and are treating this as a priority. Ben (on infra) and Marissa (customer reliability) are looped in.

Immediate steps we recommend you enable client-side while we triage: 
- Reduce your streaming chunk timeout to 45s (from 30s) and surface a soft retry at the client level after the first timeout.
- Add exponential backoff with jitter for reconnects (start 500ms, max 5s).
- Enable prefix caching for conversational contexts where possible so fewer tokens are re-sent on reconnects.
- If feasible, temporarily fall back to short-polling for sessions that have had 2 consecutive stream stalls.

We will also provision a dedicated telemetry slice to capture the exact instances tied to Novus requests and run a targeted kernel/instance health check.

Will update within 90 minutes with engineering findings.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rita Chen <rita.chen@novusretail.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live sessions sporadically slow — hitting timeouts on streaming chat

Priya / Marissa / Rita — quick technical note and what we did so far: 

What we observed: 
- Between 08:40–09:10 PDT we saw elevated tail latency on a subset of streaming frontends in us-west-2. The pattern is intermittent pauses during token emission (large gaps between stream frames) rather than continuous CPU saturation.
- Root cause (short): an interaction between a recent kernel selector heuristic and a small cohort of Llama-2-derived model shards that increased soft-lock waits when sequence-length distributions spiked. This impacted long-response sessions more.

Immediate mitigations taken (already applied):
- Rolled back the kernel selector change for the affected pool and forced a compatible kernel path for Novus's traffic ID (this lowered the pause incidence by ~70%).
- Increased per-connection streaming buffer timeout tolerances at the edge for the affected hosts to reduce client-observed timeouts while we validate.

Recommended temporary client checklist (attached as client_workarounds_checklist.pdf):
1) Increase client-side stream chunk timeout to 45s (as Priya noted).
2) Add a one-off soft retry after stream timeout returning the last acked token to the client.
3) Enable a short-poll fallback for sessions where 2 attempts to stream fail.
4) Instrument a small sampling of sessions to log last-good-ack IDs and surface that back to our incident queue.

Next steps: we are running a targeted canary with the previous kernel selector disabled and will monitor Novus traffic. Expect a follow-up with precise numbers and a patch release plan by EOD.

— Ben Carter
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Incident review & recommended next steps — Live conversation delay (May 14)

Rita — following up with a concise incident review and durable mitigations we've scheduled. Thank you for your patience and for enabling the client-side fallbacks quickly; that made the user impact materially smaller.

Summary:
- Impact window: 2027-05-14 08:40–09:20 PDT.
- Observed user impact: interleaved pauses during streaming token emission leading to ~5% session visible stalls; some sessions hit app-level timeouts prior to our buffer adjustment.
- Root cause: an unintended interaction between a kernel-selection optimization and a small subset of model shards which, under higher-than-expected long-sequence traffic patterns, increased internal soft-lock latency on certain host kernels.

What we changed (short-term):
- Rolled back the kernel selector change for impacted pools.
- Applied an instance-side patch to avoid soft-lock contention for affected model variants.
- Increased streaming buffer grace time at the edge for in-flight sessions.
- Recommended and validated your client fallback checklist — attached again for your ops team.

Planned permanent fixes (timeline):
- Engineering will publish a kernel-selection guard patch that prevents the heuristic from selecting incompatible kernel paths for long-sequence workloads (ETA: 2027-05-21).
- We'll add a regression test in our model onboarding pipeline to catch this sequence-length induced selector behavior (ETA: 2027-05-28).
- We'll surface a new telemetry counter in the Console to allow customers to filter for stream pause events per API key (ETA: 2027-06-04).

How this affects Novus:
- We've applied the rollback and patch scoped to your traffic ID; you should see normal phasing now. We'll continue 24–48h monitoring and will proactively notify you if anything unusual reappears.

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute post-incident call this week to walk through the technical changes and validate your metrics.

Thanks again — we appreciate the quick collaboration.

Best,
